note: The browser WITH its sandbox, run by a normal user, as on any Linux that allows user namespaces. On the Ubuntu 24.04 runner AppArmor refuses them to a user, so every other non-root suite runs a browser WITHOUT the sandbox of its socket and content processes; the gate turns the restriction off for this leg (sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0) and the first test fails unless the socket and a tab process have a seccomp filter (Seccomp: 2). The three situations of the UDP line: A (a proxy that carries UDP: the srflx born through the relay), B (no proxy: the gather is real), C (a proxy with no UDP: the ICE server name goes by DoH through the proxy and the gather ends in 701). No root and no resolver trap needed.
linux_only: It reads the seccomp filter of the socket and tab processes in /proc. The Windows twin reads the sandbox token of the same processes (integrity level, restrictions) and needs a measurement of the retail Firefox's tokens first; until then Linux only.

Linux needs root: the resolver trap of the file (ResolverTrap) points /etc/resolv.conf at a counting resolver on port 53. On Windows the resolver trap does not run: the system resolver assertion is the only one omitted. Run it without xdist (port 53 is one per host). On the Linux leg the gate exports INVPW_REQUIRE_TRAP=1: a trap that cannot run or bind port 53 is a failure, not a skipped assertion.

Taken from the minimal-engine port (branch tests/minimal-port) unchanged but for the removed engine gate: 12 = 6 kinds of page work (hints, image/fetch/WebSocket/EventSource, WebRTC STUN and TURN-udp by name, geolocation, a service worker with push, a page still loading when its context closes) x 2 schemes (no proxy at launch and a gateway on the context; a launch gateway and a different one on the context), and 2 = the TURN server named over TCP in those two schemes. EXPECTED RED on the published firefox-63: the 2 TURN-by-name cases (the lookup of the TCP socket takes user context 0; fixed by commits ac0214bff4 and 058edd6cc6 of firefox-64). The behavioural half of the class gate 'nothing of a context leaves but through its proxy', with a witness at an address of this host (no root, no address on lo) and the engine's own resolver log as the native-lookup sink. 35 = 31 + the 4 OCSP cases; the 31 are 19 probes (fetch, WebSocket, stun, turn over UDP, turn and turns over TCP, each by name, by IP and by a .local name, behind SOCKS5 and behind an HTTP proxy where the road differs) + 3 controls (the same probe by IP with no proxy IS heard by the witness) + 1 control of the native sink. + 4 PeerConnections built from a torn-down window (a detached iframe, a closed popup; behind SOCKS5 and behind HTTP; defect B3: EXPECTED RED on firefox-63, green on firefox-64) + 2 controls of them (the same PeerConnection from an attached iframe, green on both). + 2 cases of two contexts alive at once (each with its own proxy and DoH, a TURN server over TCP by a different name in each; behind SOCKS5 EXPECTED RED on firefox-63 like turn_tcp-name-socks5, behind HTTP green on both). EXPECTED RED on firefox-63: turn_tcp-name-socks5, turns_tcp-name-socks5 (user context 0, fixed in firefox-64) and the three .local cases fetch-local-socks5, stun-local-socks5, stun-local-http (audit B4, also red on firefox-64 until decided). The Linux leg runs as root so the resolver trap is a second sink. Windows reads the same engine log (its getaddrinfo lines are in the parent process file under the sandbox: run 43574494194), with the no-proxy native control as its positive control. THE OCSP CASES (4): a TLS page whose leaf, signed by a lab CA the engine trusts (put in the profile by the engine's xpcshell, no ignore_https_errors), names its OCSP responder by a NAME (ocsp-<nonce>.lab.test) and by an IP; a context behind the gateway loads it and the request must go through the gateway, never be looked up natively, in user context 0, or reach the responder (2 cases, EXPECTED RED on firefox-63, green on firefox-64); the same page in a context with no proxy IS asked of the responder (control); a page of an issuer the engine does not trust makes no OCSP request (negative control). THE CLOSED CONTEXT CASE (1, gated firefox-65): a beacon sent on pagehide as a proxied context closes, to a name never looked up, is resolved over the DoH through the context's gateway after the close; on firefox-64 it went to the machine's resolver every time (hunt 43733181674).

The realness check without a real proxy: six declared exits, the values a page reads, and the roads. Linux runs as root without xdist like the DoH suite (the resolver trap); on Windows the trap does not exist and the assertion on the system resolver is the only one omitted.

linux_only: Fontconfig exists only on Linux: the parent of the engine shows <GRE>/fonts to it (FcConfigAppFontAddDir) to rebuild a font from a path and a face index. On Windows DirectWrite opens the file from its path, with no folder to scan and no cache to read, so this test has no Windows counterpart.
note: 2 = (1) the stand-in that runs the engine under strace stays in the engine's place, as the core launches it (the leader of a process group of its own): a fake engine with a child, no browser; the process the launcher holds lives as long as the fake engine, and the group killed holds strace and the child (the stand-in that exec'd setsid forked and exited 0 at once: candidate 44161687675); (2) the warm launch of the parent reads the bundle from fontconfig's cache and does not scan it again (from firefox-66, engine_at_least). Two launches under strace with the same XDG_CACHE_HOME of the test, the first cold and the second warm: the cold parent opens every font file of <GRE>/fonts (the folder as the disk lists it) before any page and fontconfig writes its cache; the warm parent does not open every one of them, and it opens a *.cache-* file of fontconfig (a few files are opened to be used, so the verdict asks about the whole folder, as a scan does). Scan and drawing are told apart by position: only what the parent opens before the first page counts (the opens that draw are written as after_startup). Evidence in RUNNER_TEMP/invpw-evidence/fontconfig-cache: the interval and the number of opens of the bundle, the names of the files of the bundle each launch opened before the first page, the size of the cache file, the VmRSS of the parent after about:blank and after a page with every family, and a third launch with gfx.bundled-fonts.activate=0 (the behaviour before), which is evidence only. Needs strace on the runner: without it both are red, not skipped. No threshold.
